subject: Near-miss report: dropped timber board from north face scaffold, [AREA]
body:
**What happened**

At approximately 10:40 on Tuesday, a 300 mm length of timber board slipped from the materials hoist on the north face scaffold at level 3 of [AREA]. It fell about eight metres and landed on the exclusion barrier at ground level. Nobody was in the exclusion zone at the time and nobody was struck.

**Immediate actions**

- The exclusion zone was extended to cover the full scaffold footprint and remained in place until the bay was inspected.
- The scaffold tagging supervisor inspected the hoist and the adjacent bays. A toe board was found missing on the bay below, which is now reinstated.
- The hoist was taken out of use for the rest of the shift and returned after the scaffold inspector signed the release.

**Likely cause**

The board had been loaded on top of two other boards and was not strapped. The gang was working from a loading point that had been agreed for the earlier phase, not the current one.

**Actions for the coming week**

- Toolbox talk for all scaffold and materials handling gangs on securing loads and the hoist loading points, to be held before the next lift.
- Hoist loading point signage to be updated on each level.
- Weekly scaffold inspection to include a check of the hoist area and loading points.

Please confirm you are content with these actions so the report can be closed on the incident log.

subject: Noise complaint from residents on Harbour Lane
body:
[PM],

I have received a complaint from a resident on Harbour Lane about noise from the piling works on [SITE] over the past two weeks. The resident says the impact noise is audible inside their home with windows closed and has asked for the hours of work to be reviewed.

I would like to understand what was being done at the time of the complaint and what is planned for the next four weeks. In particular:

- the times the piling rig was running, against the hours permitted under the consent
- whether the acoustic screens on the western boundary are in place and complete
- whether a noise reading has been taken at the property boundary, and the result
- the piling programme for the remaining piles and the expected duration of each

I have asked [COW] to attend the resident's property with the monitoring team on Thursday morning, so please make sure the monitoring equipment is ready and the screens are checked beforehand. I would also like a short note from you explaining how the complaint will be logged and how you will keep the resident updated.

Please reply by close of business on Wednesday.

Regards,

[CUST_PM]

subject: Traffic management plan for site entrance, Revision C
body:
Dear [ER],

Please find enclosed Revision C of the traffic management plan for the main site entrance at [SITE]. The revision has been prepared following the trial of the temporary arrangement over the last month and comments from the local highway authority.

**Principal changes**

- The temporary give-way arrangement at the junction with the access road has been replaced by a signed stop line, with a banksman stationed at the gate during the morning and afternoon peaks.
- Delivery vehicles over 12 metres will now approach from the north only, using the revised route shown on drawing TM-03.
- A second holding area for up to four vehicles has been added inside the boundary fence, to stop vehicles queuing on the public highway.

- The speed limit within the site has been reduced to 10 mph and is signed at both entrances.

**Swept path analysis**

The swept path analysis for the largest articulated vehicles is attached as Appendix B. It confirms the revised route can be used without the vehicles crossing the centre line of the access road.

**Next steps**

We would be grateful if you could review Revision C and confirm acceptance so the banksman rota and signage can be installed before the next major delivery. Our site manager, [SITE_MGR], is available to walk the entrance with you at a time that suits.

Yours sincerely,

Brackmoor Engineering Ltd

subject: RFI: cable tray routing between MCC and pipe rack, [AREA]
body:

subject: [PROJECT] O&M manuals: agreed format and submission schedule
body:
Dear colleagues, further to the handover workshop on Tuesday, I am setting out the format we will use for the operation and maintenance manuals for the [PROJECT] plant at [SITE].

Each manual will be issued as a single PDF per system, with a master index in the front section. The structure will be:

- Section 1: system description, process flow diagram and key operating parameters
- Section 2: start-up, normal operation and shutdown procedures
- Section 3: alarm and trip schedules, with setpoints taken from the approved cause and effect matrices
- Section 4: preventive maintenance routines, lubrication schedules and spares lists
- Section 5: vendor documentation, bound in as appendices in their original form
- Section 6: certificates, test records and inspection reports

Drawing references will follow the document numbering already agreed for the project, and every page will carry the revision number and issue date. Vendor data sheets will be cross-referenced rather than reproduced in full, except where the customer's maintenance team has asked for a complete copy.

The submission schedule is as follows. Draft manuals for the gas compression package will be issued for comment on the first working day of next month, with the water treatment and substation manuals to follow two weeks later. Comments should be returned within ten working days so that final issue can be made before commissioning.

If your team has a preferred layout for the alarm schedules, please send an example and we will align the template. Regards to all.

subject: NCR close-out: weld repair documentation on the [AREA] pipework
body:
This memo records the position on the non-conformance report raised against the repair of a rejected circumferential weld on the 150 mm process line in [AREA].

**Status:** Repair complete and re-inspected. Documentation is incomplete and the NCR cannot be closed until the items below are in the file.

**Outstanding items:**

- The weld repair procedure reference has been entered on the repair record but the welder's qualification certificate for the repair operative is not attached. The certificate must show the process and position covered by the repair.
- The post-repair radiographic film has been reviewed and accepted, but the film identification number on the test report does not match the film log. Please ask the NDT subcontractor to reissue the report with the correct reference.
- The heat treatment chart is missing the thermocouple layout sketch. Without it the chart cannot be verified against the procedure.
- The grinding depth and the re-weld dimensions are recorded in millimetres on one sheet and in inches on another. One format should be used throughout.
- The hardness survey results are satisfactory but the report has not been countersigned by the authorised inspector.

**Actions:** Please have the welder certificate and the reissued radiographic report sent to the document controller by Thursday. I will walk the line again with the inspector once the heat treatment sketch and hardness report are in place.

Once all five items have been confirmed, I will sign the NCR for close-out and the record will be passed to the customer's clerk of works for their review.

subject: Amber wind warning: lifting restrictions from 06:00 tomorrow
body:
Hi [SUB_CONTACT],

The Met Office has issued an amber wind warning for the [SITE] area, covering tomorrow from 06:00 until 18:00. This affects your crews working on the modules for [AREA] and I need you to plan around the following restrictions.

From 06:00 until the warning is lifted, the following apply:

- No lifting operations with mobile cranes or the tower crane where the forecast gust speed exceeds the limit in the lift plan.
- All lifts already in progress must be brought to a safe stand-still and the load landed before the wind reaches the threshold on the site anemometer.
- Personnel must not work on the steelwork above 3 metres without fall arrest, and any work at height must be reviewed by your permit holder before it starts.
- Loose materials, scaffold boards and temporary sheeting must be secured or removed from the top lifts.
- Crane operators must confirm the anemometer reading at the start of each shift and record it on the lift log.

The site anemometer readings will be posted at the gatehouse and sent to your foreman every hour. If gusts go above the limit at any point, lifting stops immediately and the banksman will confirm the stop with me directly.

Please brief your crews at the start of the shift tomorrow and let me know by 17:00 today how many of your lifts are affected, so I can adjust the crane programme with [PLANNER].

Thanks,
[SITE_MGR]

subject: [PROJECT]: Inspection findings on welfare facilities at [SITE]
body:
Following the inspection of the welfare facilities at [SITE] carried out on Monday, I am writing to record the findings and to ask for the actions listed below.

The inspection covered the canteen, drying room, toilet and shower blocks, first aid room and the welfare cabins serving the night shift. Overall the facilities are in good order, but a number of items need attention before the next phase of the works begins.

**Findings:**

- The drying room extract fan is not running at the rated speed and the airflow is noticeably low. Please arrange an inspection by the mechanical contractor.
- Two of the shower heads on the upper floor are dripping and the water temperature at the outlet was above 50 degrees Celsius. The mixing valve should be checked and recorded.
- Hand wash basins in the north block have no soap dispensers filled, and the paper towel supply was empty at the time of inspection.
- The first aid room is clean and well stocked, but the eye wash station expiry date has passed. It should be replaced and the inspection log updated.
- The refuse store has bins without lids and the designated waste segregation labels are missing.
- The fire extinguisher in the canteen has an inspection tag more than a year old.

**Actions requested:** Please confirm by the end of next week that the items above have been rectified, with supporting photographs for the fan, the mixing valve and the eye wash replacement. A follow-up walk round will be carried out with [COW] once the confirmation is received.

I am grateful for your attention to these matters and look forward to your response.

subject: Permit-to-work audit results, [AREA], week 22
body:
## Summary

The weekly permit-to-work audit for [AREA] was carried out on Tuesday with [COW] in attendance. Eighteen live permits were sampled across hot work, confined space and lifting operations. Overall compliance was good, with no permits found in use outside their validity window.

## Findings

- **Hot work:** Two fire watch logs were completed after the task ended but not at the time of completion. Both supervisors have been reminded.
- **Isolations:** One lock-off certificate had the wrong tag reference. The correct tag was confirmed on site and the record has been amended.
- **Gas testing:** All gas test readings were recorded at the required intervals and signed.
- **Housekeeping:** Two work areas beside the pipe rack had trip hazards from unused scaffold tube. These were cleared before the end of the shift.

## Actions

1. Permit issuers to complete fire watch entries at the point the task finishes, not at the end of the shift.
2. Isolation tags to be checked against the permit register at the morning briefing.
3. Area supervisors to walk their work front at 14:00 each day to check for loose materials.

The next audit is scheduled for the same day next week. Please let me know if you would like the full sample list for your records.

subject: CDM principal designer coordination meeting: minutes and actions
body:
Dear colleague,

Thank you for attending the principal designer coordination meeting on Thursday. I have set out below the points we discussed and the actions agreed. Please review them and let me know by the end of next week if anything is inaccurate or incomplete.

## Design information

The design team confirmed that the revised general arrangement drawings for the tie-in area have been issued for construction. Any earlier drawing revisions held on site should be withdrawn and marked superseded. Brackmoor will confirm the site copy register is up to date.

Kind regards in advance for your attention to these points.

subject: Crane lift plan review for [AREA] pipe rack sections
body:
Hi,

Further to our discussion at the morning meeting, I have now completed the review of the lift plan for the pipe rack sections in [AREA]. The main points are below.

The lift weights have been checked against the rigging schedule and the load chart for the 250 tonne crane. The heaviest pick is 14.2 tonnes including the spreader beam, which leaves an acceptable margin at the proposed radius. The outrigger mats were confirmed as suitable for the ground bearing pressure shown on the ground survey.

Two points need attention before the first lift:

1. The exclusion zone on the lift plan does not match the marked-up site plan. It needs to extend to the west side of the drain run, which is currently shown as outside the zone.
2. The banksman position needs to be confirmed. The plan shows one banksman at ground level, but the pick point is visible only from the top of the rack. A second signaller is required at that location.

I would also like the lift supervisor to walk the route with the operator before the first pick, and to record the wind limit that will be used for the operation.

The revised plan will be sent over once the exclusion zone is corrected. Please let me know if you want a call before then.

Regards

subject: Dust monitoring results at site boundary, last four weeks
body:
Hi,

I have reviewed the dust monitoring results for the four monitoring points on the site boundary for the last four weeks. The summary is below for information.

All readings were within the trigger levels set in the dust management plan. The highest 24-hour average at any point was recorded at the south gate monitor, on the day the concrete breaking started. The reading was below the action level, but it was higher than the other points and is worth keeping an eye on while that activity continues.

The north and east monitors showed low readings throughout, which is consistent with the wind direction recorded on site for most of the period. The west monitor was out of service for two days because of a power interruption. The data logger has been reset and readings have resumed.

The following points are recommended:

- Dampen the haul road at the south gate before concrete breaking starts each morning.
- Keep the wheel wash running during the first hour of each shift, when vehicle movements are highest.
- Record the wind speed and direction against each breaking activity so that any future exceedance can be traced more easily.

I will post the full data set to the shared folder by Monday so that the environmental team can check it against the permit conditions.

Thanks

subject: Archaeological watching brief update, [SITE] access road
body:
Dear [ER],

I am writing to update you on the archaeological watching brief for the new access road at [SITE]. The archaeologist appointed under the written scheme of investigation has been on site for the groundworks in the north-west corner since the start of the month.

## Progress

Topsoil stripping has been completed across the section between chainage 0 and chainage 180. The archaeologist observed the works and recorded the exposed surface. No significant archaeological deposits were found in this section. A small quantity of modern brick and clay pipe fragments was recovered from the topsoil and has been bagged for the record.

## Findings

At chainage 220, a linear feature was exposed beneath the subsoil. The archaeologist has recorded it in plan and section and has advised that it may be a field boundary. Further excavation has been paused at this point to allow the feature to be recorded fully. The works have been re-sequenced so that the adjacent drainage trench can proceed while the recording is completed.

## Next steps

- The archaeologist will complete the record for the linear feature by the end of next week.
- Brackmoor will keep the watching brief in place for all ground disturbance within the defined area.
- A written summary will be issued to the county archaeology team once the fieldwork is complete.

I will send you the recording sheets and photographs when they are available. Please let me know if you would like to visit the trench before it is backfilled.

Yours sincerely

subject: [PROJECT] - Planned electrical outage coordination for tie-in works at [AREA]
body:

subject: [PROJECT] - Attempted theft of copper earthing cable, night of 3rd to 4th
body:
Dear [ER],

I am writing to report an attempted theft of copper earthing cable from the cable tray route on the east side of [SITE], discovered by the night security patrol at approximately 02:40 on the morning of 4th.

From the initial inspection, the perimeter fence had been cut at the access gate to the laydown area, and a section of approximately 15 metres of tray-mounted earthing conductor had been partly stripped and cut. The cable had not been removed from the site. The local police attended, took a statement and have given us a crime reference number, which I have attached.

**Immediate actions taken**

- The affected section has been isolated and made safe by our electrical team, with a permit to work issued.
- The gate and fence have been repaired temporarily and a temporary security barrier installed.
- Additional mobile patrols have been put in place for the next two weeks, covering the laydown area and the cable routes.
- All cable reels and loose copper stock in the laydown area have been moved into the secured compound.

**Actions to follow**

We will carry out a full inspection of the earthing system before re-energising the affected section, with the results recorded on the commissioning certificate. A review of the access control arrangements at the gate will be held with [CUST_PM] next Tuesday.

I will confirm the outcome of the inspection in writing once it is complete.

Yours sincerely

subject: Temporary works design check certificate - Level 3 propping, east pipe rack
body:
Hi [SITE_MGR],

The temporary works design check for the propping arrangement to the east pipe rack is now complete. The independent checker's certificate is attached, signed and dated this morning.

- The inspection record must be completed by a competent person before each loading stage, and the tag system should be in place at the access points.
- The checker has asked to see the first prop installed before the rest of the bay is started, so please give us the day.
- The lifting plan for the props is still with us for review, and I will send it over on Monday.

We are ready to start erection on Wednesday if the platform is confirmed as finished. Could you let me know by Tuesday afternoon whether the platform inspection has been signed off?

Regards

subject: [PROJECT] - Commissioning sequence workshop, invitation and agenda
body:
Dear [CUST_PM],

We would like to hold a commissioning sequence workshop on Thursday 19th, from 09:30 to 13:00, in the site meeting room. The purpose is to agree the order in which the systems at [AREA] will be energised, tested and handed over, and to identify any points where one system depends on another.

**Proposed agenda**

2. Utilities required in advance: power, instrument air, nitrogen and cooling water.
3. Sequence for the water systems, including flushing, hydrotesting and drying out.
4. Sequence for the rotating equipment, including alignment checks and dry runs.
5. Interface points with the operating team and their permit requirements.
6. Actions and owners.

I would be grateful if [COW] could attend for the first and fifth items in particular, as the permit interface is where most of the open questions sit. The workshop will be chaired by [PLANNER], who has the latest version of the sequence logic.

Please confirm your attendance and let us know if any of your team need to join by video. I have attached the draft systems list so that you can mark up any missing items before the day.

With thanks

body:

subject: Site hoarding branding at [SITE]
body:

subject: Car park arrangements from Monday
body:

- Bays 1 to 40 are reserved for Brackmoor staff and subcontractor supervisors holding a permit.
- Vans and minibuses are to park in bays 41 to 55, nearest the gate.

subject: Bank holiday working hours over the Easter weekend
body:
**Purpose**

This memo sets out the working arrangements for Good Friday and Easter Monday. The customer's site rules do not permit unrestricted working on public holidays, so the arrangements below must be followed.

**Permitted hours**

- Good Friday: no site working. Security patrols and plant monitoring only.
- Easter Monday: 07:00 to 15:00, with a reduced crew of no more than twelve.

**Restrictions on Easter Monday**

- No crane lifts or lifting operations.
- No hot work, grinding or hydro-testing.
- No noisy activities, including breaking out, piling or jackhammering, before 08:00.
- Every task requires a permit to work signed by the duty supervisor.

**Actions**

Please confirm the crew list to me by Wednesday. [CUST_PM] has yet to confirm the customer's attendance, so hold the plan as provisional until I have their written agreement. Security will need the gate rota updated, and the duty engineer must be named on the emergency contact sheet.

If any of the planned work cannot be completed within the permitted hours, raise it with me immediately so that we can reprioritise the sequence rather than work outside the agreed times.

subject: Waste transfer notes and skip segregation at [AREA]
body:
Following Thursday's housekeeping walk, I have set out how we will segregate waste at [AREA] from next week. There are now four skips on the lay-down area, each clearly labelled:

- Clean timber
- Ferrous and non-ferrous metal
- Mixed inert (concrete, brick and rubble)
- Hazardous (contaminated lagging, oily rags and used absorbent)

The hazardous skip must be lidded and stood on the drip tray at all times. It must not be used for general rubbish.

A waste transfer note will be completed for every collection. Our driver and your site representative will both sign it at the point of handover, and I will send you a copy the same day. For the hazardous skip, we will also provide a consignment note, which must be retained with the site waste file. Please make sure your operatives know that nothing goes into a skip without a labelled container first.

Could you confirm the named person on your side who will sign the notes? Our crews will not load until that person has been confirmed.

subject: Fire evacuation drill report, [AREA]
body:
I observed the fire evacuation drill for [AREA] carried out last Thursday. The alarm was raised at 10:15 and the building was cleared in good order. The principal findings are set out below.

**Observations**

- Roll call was completed in 11 minutes and 40 seconds. The target is 10 minutes.
- Two contractors were not on the signing-in register and could not be accounted for at the assembly point until their names were checked against the gate log.
- The fire door in the compressor house was propped open with a wooden wedge. This would have compromised the compartment.
- The extinguisher at bay 4 was past its inspection date.
- Two of the four marshals were not wearing hi-vis and were not identifiable to the crowd.
- The assembly point at the north gate was clear and well signed.

**Actions requested**

Please arrange for the compressor house door to be fitted with a free-closing device and the extinguisher replaced before the next drill. Marshals should be issued with fresh hi-vis and briefed on their roles. The signing-in register should be checked against the gate log at the start of each shift.

I would be grateful for written confirmation of these actions by the end of the month, together with the date of the next drill, so that [CUST_PM] can attend.

subject: Document control procedure update, Revision C
body:
**Purpose**

The document control procedure for [PROJECT] has been revised to Revision C. It takes effect from Monday and replaces Revision B in full. Controlled copy holders will receive the new issue through the document management system, and paper copies held at the [SITE] document hub will be swapped on the same day.

**Key changes**

- Every transmittal must quote the current document register number and revision letter. Transmittals without these will be returned unactioned.
- Superseded markups and redlines are to be moved to the site records store within two working days of a revised issue being received.
- Issued-for-construction drawings printed for the field must carry the stamp and be logged on the hub sheet before they leave the document room.
- Vendor documents for [AREA] are routed through the engineering team for review before issue to site, not sent direct.

**Actions**

subject: Lessons learned following minor collision on [AREA]
body:
Hi [SITE_MGR],

Thank you for the time you took to walk the site with my team on Tuesday after the telehandler contact with the pipe rack. I have now completed our internal review and wanted to share the main points so they can go into the next toolbox talk.

What happened: the operator was reversing a loaded pallet out of the laydown bay and did not have a banksman in place. The reversing alarm was working, but the rear view was blocked by the load. The contact damaged one pipe support bracket, with no injuries and no leak.

What we have changed:
- A banksman is now mandatory for any reversing move in a congested area, regardless of distance
- Loads must be sited so the operator has a clear rear view before lifting
- The laydown bay has been re-marked with exclusion lines to keep foot traffic away from the reversing path
- Our daily plant checks now include a camera and mirror test

What we would like from the wider site: a short reminder to all plant operators in the next briefing, and a request to [COW] to add the bay marking to the weekly inspection checklist.

The damaged bracket has been reported to your team and I understand it has already been replaced.

Kind regards,

**Date and time:** Tuesday, 07:40, during the morning toolbox start.

**What happened:** A scaffold tie clip fell from the working lift on the north face of [AREA] at level 2. It landed on the hardstanding approximately 3 metres from a welder who was setting up his equipment. Nobody was struck.

**Immediate actions taken:**

- Exclusion zone extended to 6 metres around the north elevation.
- Scaffold inspected by the scaffold sub-contractor's tagged inspector before work resumed at 10:15.
- Loose tools and fittings on the affected lift cleared and retained as evidence.
- Toe boards and mesh checked along the full lift length.

**Likely cause:** The tie clip was not secured to the lift board after the previous shift's handover. The lift had been partly stripped and left unattended overnight.

**Proposed actions:**

1. Reminder at tomorrow's toolbox talk that all loose fittings must be bagged and tagged before leaving a lift.
2. Scaffold handover checklist to be signed by both outgoing and incoming supervisors.
3. Daily walk-down of the north face by the scaffold supervisor for the next two weeks.

body:
Hi [PM],

We are preparing the cable tray installation drawings for the [AREA] pipe bridge and have found a conflict that we need resolved before we can fix the supports.

As currently drawn, the main 600 mm cable tray runs through the same bay as the 12-inch process line on grid C4. There is not enough clearance between the bottom of the pipe insulation and the top of the tray to maintain the minimum separation shown in the electrical specification.

We have identified three possible routes:

1. Drop the tray by 300 mm at grid C4 and run it under the pipe, with a short ladder rack transition at each end.
2. Move the tray to the outside of the bridge, on the cantilever bracket, which would need additional support steel.
3. Split the tray into two 300 mm trays running either side of the pipe.

Option 1 looks the most straightforward to us, but we need the engineering position on the minimum separation and whether the piping team is content with the revised support loads.

Could you raise this as a formal request for information with the design team and let us have a response by Thursday? We have a crew booked on this bay from Monday, so we need to be ready to start on the supports.

Thanks,

[SUB_CONTACT]

subject: Format of operation and maintenance manuals for [AREA]
body:
This memo sets out the format agreed for the operation and maintenance manuals for [AREA], so that the sections can be drafted consistently by each discipline.

**File format**

- Each manual is to be issued as a single PDF with bookmarks linked to the main headings.
- Files must be named using the pattern [PROJECT]-[AREA]-OM-XX, where XX is the volume number.
- Drawings are to be included in A3 format, folded to A4 and placed at the back of each volume.

**Structure**

1. Introduction and scope
2. Safety information and permits to work
3. Equipment descriptions, using the tag numbers from the master equipment list
4. Operating procedures, including start-up, shutdown and emergency isolation
5. Maintenance schedules and task sheets
6. Spare parts lists with supplier references
7. Certificates, test records and inspection reports

**Numbering and tagging**

- Equipment tag numbers must match the P&ID and the equipment register exactly. Do not abbreviate them.
- Page numbers should restart in each section.
- Revision history goes on the inside cover of each volume.

**Programme**

- Draft volumes 1 and 2 are due to [CUST_PM] by the end of next week.
- Volumes 3 to 5 follow two weeks after that.
- Each draft must be checked by the discipline lead before it is passed to document control.

Please send any questions to me directly. If a section cannot be completed because vendor data is still outstanding, flag it in the draft rather than leaving it blank.

The repair cavity dimensions on the weld map do not match the measurements recorded in the repair log. Please check these and confirm which set is correct, with a short note explaining the difference.

subject: Amber weather warning and high-wind lifting restrictions
body:
The Met Office has issued an amber weather warning for the site area from 14:00 tomorrow until 06:00 on Thursday. Your crews must apply the following restrictions from the moment the warning takes effect.

**Lifting operations**

- All crane lifts must stop when the site anemometer on the north gantry reads a sustained wind speed of 20 mph or gusts above 30 mph.
- Lifts that are already under way must be lowered to a safe position and secured before the crew leaves the lift.
- Loads with a large sail area, such as cladding panels or sheet material, must not be lifted at any wind speed above 15 mph.
- Banksmen must check the wind readings on the display at the start of every lift and log them on the permit.

**Work at height**

- Work on scaffolding, cherry pickers and steel erection above 10 metres must stop when the wind exceeds 25 mph.
- All scaffold tags should be checked before the warning starts, and any loose boards or ties reported to [PM].

**Housekeeping**

- Secure all loose materials, sheeting, and temporary signs before 14:00.
- Empty skips and store small tools in lockable containers.
- Check that the tower lights and barriers around [AREA] are still in place.

**Monitoring**

- The site team will check the forecast at 06:00 and again at 12:00 each day while the warning is active.
- Your supervisor must confirm to me by text when your crew has stopped and secured the work.

Please brief your operatives at the morning meeting tomorrow and sign the sheet to confirm that they have understood these restrictions.

subject: Crane lift plan review, heat exchanger shell lift
body:
Following the review meeting on Monday, please find below the points raised on the draft lift plan for the heat exchanger shell lift on [AREA]. The lift is to be made with our 350 tonne crawler crane and the shell weighs approximately 42 tonnes including rigging.

**Points to close before the lift**

- Ground bearing: the bearing capacity of the crane pad needs to be confirmed on the ground investigation report. Our engineer has asked for the mat specification to be checked against the outrigger loads shown on page 6.
- Exclusion zone: the zone shown on the drawing does not include the pipe rack access route. This must be extended and marked on site before the crane is erected.
- Slinging arrangement: the revised sling angles give a lower safety factor on the chokers than the original plan. We have proposed a spreader beam, which is shown in the attached sketch.
- Wind limits: the lift will stop if the wind exceeds 10 metres per second at the boom head. A wind gauge should be mounted on the crane at the point of the lift and read by the lift supervisor.
- Tag lines: two tag lines are required on the shell. The banksmen should be identified by name on the permit before the day of the lift.

**Documents needed**

Please send the load test certificate for the spreader beam and the latest inspection report for the crane. We also need confirmation that the lift supervisor and the appointed person will both be on site for the full duration.

We can be ready to make the lift on the planned date if these points are closed by Thursday. Please call me if any of the items need discussing before then.

subject: Dust monitoring results at the site boundary, four-week period
body:
I write to share the results of the dust monitoring carried out at the site boundary over the last four weeks. Four continuous monitors have been operating along the boundary fence at [SITE], one on each side of the compound, and the readings have been logged against the agreed trigger levels.

**Summary of results**

Daily mean PM10 readings stayed below the agreed trigger level on all days except one. The exception occurred on the Thursday of the second week, when excavation on the north haul road coincided with a period of dry, windy weather. The monitor on the north fence recorded a daily mean above the trigger level for that single day.

The readings for the other three monitors remained well within the limits throughout the period, and no reading on any monitor recorded a one-hour exceedance.

**Action taken**

On the day of the exceedance, the haul road was watered by a bowser every hour and the excavation was paused during the strongest gusts. A wind-speed alarm has since been added to the excavation procedure, so that work stops automatically when the on-site anemometer reads above the set limit. The water bowser schedule has been increased for dry weather, and the haul road surface is being treated with a dust suppressant from the coming week.

The monitoring data, the calibration certificates and the wind records for the period are enclosed. [SITE_MGR] will continue to review the readings each week and will alert you directly if any trigger level is approached.

Please let me know if you would like the monitoring frequency increased for the next phase of excavation works.

subject: Archaeological watching brief update, week 11
body:
This memo gives an update on the archaeological watching brief for the works within [AREA] this week. The brief is being carried out by the archaeologist from [SUB] under the agreed written scheme of investigation, and the county archaeologist has been kept informed throughout.

**Findings this week**

- Trench 4, on the eastern edge of the cable route, exposed a ditch running roughly north to south. The fill contained a small number of medieval pottery sherds and a fragment of animal bone.
- The finds have been bagged, labelled and recorded on the find sheet. They are held in the finds tray in the site office, and the tray must not be moved without the archaeologist's signature.
- No human remains have been found so far on the route.

**Working arrangements**

The exclusion zone around Trench 4 is to remain in place until the archaeologist has completed the recording, which is expected by Wednesday. Excavation for the drainage run in grid line C is to be monitored by the archaeologist on the day, and the machine operator should stop work immediately if any layer of dark soil or unusual material is exposed.

Piling on grid line C is planned for next week. The archaeologist will need to attend the first two piles, and the piling subcontractor should be told the start time in advance so that the attendance can be arranged.

**Actions**

- [SITE_MGR] to brief the drainage gang on the stop-work requirement before Monday's start.
- The archaeologist to send the interim findings report to [CUST_PM] by Friday.
- I will walk the route with [SUB] on Tuesday morning to confirm the revised boundary of the exclusion zone.

subject: Attempted theft of copper earth cable, cable drum store, 9 May
body:
At 02:40 on Friday 9 May, the night security patrol found a section of the south perimeter fence cut open beside the cable drum store. A length of 70mm2 copper earth cable had been partly cut from a drum and pulled towards the fence. The patrol saw two individuals leaving along the access road with their vehicle lights off, and they did not stop when challenged.

The cable was not removed from site. The cut section is approximately three metres long and has been retained for inspection. The police attended at 03:15 and have issued crime reference 4417/0509. A copy of the reference is attached.

Actions taken so far:

- Fence breach made secure with temporary Heras panels and a fence inspection logged
- Temporary lighting installed along the south fence and at the cable store
- Patrol frequency increased to every 90 minutes overnight
- CCTV camera at gate 2 repositioned to cover the drum store approach
- Full inventory check of cable drums completed on Friday morning, with no other losses found

I will arrange a permanent fence repair with [SUB] for next week and will send the completed inspection report on Monday. Could you confirm whether the customer's security team wishes to review the incident log before we close it out?

subject: Temporary works design check certificate, propping scheme for pipe rack beam lift, bay 3
body:

If your team has any questions on the scheme, please let me know by Wednesday so the review can be completed before the planned lift date. I am happy to arrange a short walk-down with the checker if that would help.

subject: Carbon reporting return: data needed by Friday
body:

subject: Draft content for the community liaison newsletter, issue 4
body:
## Purpose

The next community liaison newsletter goes to residents, the parish council and local businesses on the route of the access road. It needs to be issued by the end of the month. The customer's community team has approved the format, so the content below is the draft for your review.

## Proposed content

**Progress on site**
The foundations for the new compressor building are complete. Steelwork erection will start in the next fortnight and will be visible from the public footpath on the north side of the site.

**Working hours and deliveries**
Deliveries are restricted to 08:00 to 18:00 on weekdays and 08:00 to 13:00 on Saturdays. Night deliveries are not planned for this period. Any change will be notified in advance.

**Traffic management**
The temporary traffic lights on the B-road will be moved on the 14th. Diversion signs will be in place from the Monday before.

**Noise**
The piling work is finished. The remaining noisy activities are the concrete pours and the crane lifts. We will give residents at least 48 hours' notice of any night working.

**How to contact us**
The community helpline and the email address for complaints will be printed in the back page, along with the site office opening hours.

## Actions

Please check the traffic dates and the steelwork timing with the planner before the draft goes to the customer. Send any photographs for the progress section to me by Friday. I will then forward the full draft to [CUST_PM] for comment.

subject: Approval of paint samples for [AREA] external pipework
body:
Further to the sample panels delivered to the site office on Tuesday, I have reviewed the three proposed topcoat systems for the external pipework in [AREA].

System B, the epoxy mid-coat with polyurethane finish in RAL 7032, meets the colour and gloss targets set out in the painting specification. I am content for this system to be taken forward for the remaining pipe spools.

Systems A and C are not accepted. The gloss level on A falls outside the specified tolerance at the 60 degree reading, and the colour on C drifts noticeably under daylight compared with the reference chip. Please do not use either system on any further works.

Before application begins, I would ask for the following:

- Written confirmation of the batch numbers for System B, matching the samples retained on site.
- Dry film thickness readings from the trial area, taken at the three locations marked on the drawing.
- Confirmation that surface preparation to St 2 standard is recorded for each spool before coating.

[COW] will witness the first two spool coats and sign the inspection record accordingly. Please give [COW] at least one working day's notice before coating starts so that the hold point can be scheduled.

I would be grateful for a short reply confirming receipt and the programme for the first application.

subject: Invitation to witness hydrostatic test, flowline FL-07 in [AREA]
body:

subject: Concrete cube test results, compressor foundation pour CF-14
body:
We write to share the cube test results for pour CF-14, the compressor skid foundation placed on 3 March. The concrete was specified as C40/50 with a maximum water-cement ratio of 0.45.

The seven-day results from the independent laboratory are as follows:

| Cube ID | Age (days) | Compressive strength (MPa) |
|---|---|---|
| CF14-A | 7 | 36.8 |
| CF14-B | 7 | 38.1 |
| CF14-C | 7 | 35.9 |

The mean of the three cubes is 36.9 MPa, which is in line with the expected early-age gain for this mix. The 28-day cubes will be tested on 31 March, and we will issue the full laboratory report, reference LAB-25-0417, once it is received.

Slump on arrival was recorded at 110 mm on each batch ticket, and the curing regime of wet hessian and polythene sheeting has been maintained since placing. [COW] has the batch tickets and the temperature log for the pour and will make them available on request.

We will advise you of any change to the 28-day programme. The formwork strip date remains unchanged, subject to your team's agreement.

subject: Lightning protection inspection results, tank farm TF-2
body:
Hi,

We completed the lightning protection inspection on the tank farm TF-2 earthing and bonding network yesterday. Summary below, with the full test sheets to follow by Friday.

**Earth electrode resistance**
- Tank 2A pit: 3.2 ohms
- Tank 2B pit: 4.1 ohms
- Bund drain bond: 2.8 ohms

All readings are within the design limit of 10 ohms.

**Continuity**
- Bonding between the roof shell and the earth bar on Tank 2A passed.
- Bonding on Tank 2B passed after one clamp was re-torqued.
- Flange bonding across the pipework manifold is still to be checked on the east run, as the bonding straps are not yet fitted.

**Observations**
- One air terminal on the vent mast has a loose fixing bolt. We have tightened it, but the mast should be inspected again after the next high wind.
- Two test links are missing their protective covers.

The inspection certificate can be issued once the east manifold straps are fitted and checked. Could you confirm when [SITE] can allow access to that section, ideally before Wednesday?

Thanks,
[SUB_CONTACT]

subject: Reminder: personal protective equipment standards on [SITE]
body:
This memo is a routine reminder of the minimum personal protective equipment (PPE) standards that apply across [SITE]. Please share it with all operatives on your next toolbox talk and confirm that it has been done.

**Minimum requirements in all work areas**

- Safety helmets to EN 397, with chin straps fitted when working at height or in wind
- Safety footwear to EN ISO 20345, rated S3 as a minimum
- High-visibility clothing to EN ISO 20471, Class 2 minimum, worn at all times outside site offices
- Eye protection to EN 166 for any cutting, grinding, chipping or pressurised testing

**Additional requirements by task**

- Hearing protection to EN 352 within the marked noise zones in [AREA]
- Gloves suited to the task, with chemical-resistant gloves for flushing and hydrotesting
- Fall arrest harnesses inspected before each use, with the inspection tag recorded

**Checks**

The site team will carry out spot checks each morning this week. Operatives found without the correct PPE will be stood down until it is corrected, and the incident will be logged on the daily report.

If any of your operatives have damaged or expired PPE, please replace it before they start work. Our stores can issue replacements on request.

Please direct any questions to me in the site office.
